history.summary: The 4th of the 12 Jyotirlingas, on Mandhata Island — naturally shaped like the Om symbol — in the Narmada river, Khandwa district. Legends tie it to King Mandhata of the Ikshvaku dynasty, who performed penance here, and to the Vindhya mountain's worship of Shiva. Inscriptions of King Udayaditya (1063) are recorded at the site; Raja Bharat Singh Chauhan renovated the temple in 1195. The twin shrine Mamleshwar (seq 1812, also called Amareshwar) stands on the mainland south bank; tradition says a pilgrimage is complete only after visiting both, Mamleshwar first. The temple is Nagara-style with intricate carvings; smaller shrines to Ganesha, Parvati and Kartikeya stand in the complex, and a Narmada Aarti is held daily on the river bank. Note: the geocoder's 'Omkareshwar Road' locality is in Khandwa district; coordinates are for the island temple itself.

name: Shri Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga Temple
town_description: Omkareshwar is a small pilgrimage town in Khandwa district built around the Om-shaped Mandhata Island in the Narmada river, site of one of the twelve Jyotirlingas. A bridge connects the mainland to the island, and a 7-8 km parikrama path circles the island past many small shrines. The town also holds the Mamleshwar temple on the south bank, Kedareshwar and Gauri Somnath temples, and daily Narmada aarti at the ghats. It is about 77 km from Indore, the usual gateway.
